semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ}: The majority read it with kasra on the tāʾ (تِسْع), which is the widespread dialect. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and al-Ḥasan read it with fatḥa on both (تَسْع), which is a minor dialect. The majority read «نَعْجة» with fatḥa on the nūn, while al-Ḥasan and Ibn Hurmuz read it with kasra (نِعْجة); it is said that this is the dialect of some of Banū Tamīm. It is common in their speech to use it as a euphemism for a woman. Ibn ʿAwn said:

3858 - I am the father of them, three, they are (hunnah) ... a fourth in the house, the youngest of them (ṣughrāhunnah) ... and my ewe (naʿjatī) — five whom you will fulfil to them (tuwaffīhinnah) ... (Translator's note: the verse is quoted as it appears in the source, where the lines are run together and the text is evidently corrupt; the gloss is tentative.) And another said:

3859 - They are two ewes (naʿjatān) of the ewes of Tabāla ... beside two fawns or like some marble statues of Hakir.

His saying: «وعَزَّني» means "he overcame me". The poet said:

3860 - A sand-grouse that a snare (sharak) overpowered (ʿazzahā), so she spent the night ... struggling against it, her wing caught fast. (Translator's note: the gloss is tentative.)

One says: ʿazzahu yaʿuzzuhu, with ḍamma on the ʿayn; its verification came earlier in Sūrat Yā Sīn. Ṭalḥa and Abū Ḥaywa read «وَعَزَنِي» with lightening (a single zāy). Ibn Jinnī said: "One zāy is dropped for lightness, as he said:

3861 - ... They sensed him (aḥasna bihi), and they turned towards him in sullen aversion (shūs)

meaning aḥsasna, and he dropped one letter." This is also reported as a reading from ʿĀṣim. ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd), al-Ḥasan, Abū Wāʾil, Masrūq and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «وعازَّني» with an alif and doubled zāy, that is, "he contended with me to overcome me".

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {بِسُؤَالِ نَعْجَتِكَ}: A maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its object; the agent is omitted, i.e. "by his asking you for your ewe". The asking is made to include the sense of adding and joining, i.e. "by adding your ewe to his own by way of asking", and for that reason it is made transitive with إلى.

His saying: «لَيَبْغي»: The majority read it with sukūn on the yāʾ, and it is an imperfect verb, nominative, in the position of the predicate of «إنَّ». It was also read «لَيَبْغيَ» with fatḥa on both yāʾs. This is explained by saying that the original is لَيَبْغِيَنْ with the light nūn of emphasis, the verb being the answer to an implied oath, and the implied oath together with its answer being the predicate of «إنَّ», the implied form being: "and many of the partners, by Allah, will surely wrong"; the nūn was then omitted, as it was omitted in his saying:

3862 - Strike (iḍribā) from yourself the cares, the one that visits at night ... ...

And «ألم نَشْرَحَ» was read with fatḥa (on the ḥāʾ), and his saying:

3863 - From the day it was not decreed, or the day it was decreed (qudir) ... with fatḥa on the rāʾ. And «لَيَبْغِ» was read with the yāʾ omitted. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He was content with the kasra in place of it." And the Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "like his saying:

3864 - Muḥammad, may you ransom (tafdi) yourself, every soul ... ...

meaning tafdī, on one of two views" — that is, he omitted the yāʾ, being content with the kasra in place of it. The second view is that it is jussive by an implied lām of command. This has already been discussed in Sūrat Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, except that it cannot work here because the lām is with fatḥa.

His saying: {إِلاَّ الذين آمَنُواْ}: A connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil) from his saying «بعضهم». And his saying «وقليلٌ» is a fronted khabar, and «ما» is redundant (for magnification); «هم» is the mubtadaʾ.

His saying: «فَتَنَّاه» with lightening (fatannāhu): attributing it to the pronoun of the speaker who magnifies himself is the reading of the majority. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ read «فَتَّنَّاه» with doubling of the tāʾ, which is intensification. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «أفتنَّاه»; one says fatanahu and aftanahu, meaning "he induced him to temptation (fitna)". From it is his saying:

3865 - If she has tempted me, she had tempted (aftanat) yesterday ... ...

Qatāda and Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, read «فَتَناه» with lightening, and «فتنَّاه» with doubling, the alif being the pronoun of the two litigants. And «راكِعاً» is a ḥāl muqaddara (an anticipated circumstantial), as Abū al-Baqāʾ said. There is some doubt about this, since coincidence in time is evident.

semin-durr:25-25.t: His saying: {ذَلِكَ}: Apparently it is the object of «غَفَرْنا». Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that it be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is that" — but what need is there for this?

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {فَيُضِلَّكَ}: There are two views on it. The more apparent is that it is accusative in the answer to a prohibition. The second is that it is conjoined to «لا تَتَّبِعْ», so it is jussive, and the lām has fatḥa only because of the meeting of two sukūns. In that case it is a prohibition of each of the two separately, whereas the first view prohibits combining the two. The second may be preferred for this meaning. The explanation of this has already been given in al-Baqara, in his saying {وَتَكْتُمُواْ الحق} [al-Baqara: 42]. The agent of «فَيُضِلَّك» may be «الهوى», or it may be the pronoun of the maṣdar understood from the verb, i.e. "following desire will lead you astray". The majority read «يَضِلُّون» with fatḥa; Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan and Abū Ḥaywa read «يُضِلُّون» with ḍamma, i.e. "they lead people astray". This entails the first reading, since only one who is himself astray leads another astray, and not the reverse.

His saying: «بما نَسُوا»: «ما» is maṣdarī (a maṣdar-forming particle). The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the existence (istiqrār) implied by «لهم». And «لهم عذابٌ» may be a clause serving as the predicate of «إنَّ», or the predicate may be the preposition and its genitive noun alone. «عذابٌ» is then the agent of it (of the implied verb in the prepositional phrase), and this is the better view because of its closeness to the single word (mufrad).

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {بَاطِلاً}: It may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, or a ḥāl from its pronoun, i.e. "a vain creation"; it may be a ḥāl from the agent of «خَلَقْنا», i.e. "acting in vain" or "possessing vanity"; and it may be a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for vanity", which is idle play. «أم» in both places is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, and you already know what is said about it.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {كِتَابٌ}: It may be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "this is a Book", with «أَنْزَلْناه» as an adjective and «مبارَكٌ» as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, or as a second khabar. It cannot be a second adjective, because according to the majority a non-explicit (clausal) adjective is not placed before an explicit one; those who allow it rely on the apparent form of the verse. This has already been settled in al-Māʾida.

And «لِيَدَّبَّروا» is attached to «أَنْزَلْناه». «مبارَكاً» was also read, as an inseparable ḥāl, because blessing never leaves it. ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, read «لِيَتَدَبَّروا», which is the origin of the majority reading, the tāʾ being assimilated into the dāl. Abū Jaʿfar — and it is also reported from ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī — read «لِتَدَبَّروا» with the tāʾ of the second person and lightening of the dāl. Its original is لِتَتَدَبَّروا with two tāʾs, one of which was dropped. Here the well-known disagreement applies: is it the first or the second?

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {نِعْمَ العبد}: Its specified subject of praise (makhṣūṣ) is omitted, i.e. "an excellent servant is Solomon". It is also said: David. The first is more apparent, because he is the one about whom the account is being told. It was also read with kasra on the ʿayn (niʿma), which is the original, as in his saying:

3866 - ... ... How excellent (niʿima) are those who strive among the people, the shaven-headed (?) (Translator's note: the verse is incomplete in the source and the final word is obscure; gloss tentative.)

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {إِذْ عُرِضَ}: There are several views on what governs it. One: «نِعْم»; this is the weakest, because his praise is not restricted to a time, and because niʿma is not conjugated. Two: «أوَّاب», which restricts his description to this time. Three: an implied "remember", which is the soundest. «الصَّافِناتُ» is the plural of ṣāfin. There is a disagreement about it among the linguists. Al-Zajjāj said: it is the one that stands on one of its forelegs and on the tip of its hoof, and it may do that with one of its hind legs. He said: "That is a sign of its excellence." And he cited:

3867 - He has grown used to standing on three legs (al-ṣufūn), so he is never but as if ... from standing on three, broken (Translator's note: gloss tentative.)

It is also said: it is the one that brings its forelegs together and levels them; as for the one that stands on the tip of its hoof, its name is al-mukhīm, said Abū ʿUbayd. It is also said: it is simply the one standing, whether among horses or other animals, said by al-Qutabī, who adduced the ḥadīth, the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: "Whoever is pleased that people should stand in rows (ṣufūnan) for him, let him take his seat in the Fire", i.e. that they keep standing for him. Quṭrub also related it. And it is said: it is standing in general, whether one stands on the tip of the hoof or not. Al-Farrāʾ said: "On this I have seen the poetry of the Arabs." End of quotation. Al-Nābigha said:

3868 - We have a tent pitched at its courtyard ... noble riding camels and the standing (al-ṣawāfin) thoroughbreds

And «الجِيادُ»: either from jawda (excellence) — one says jāda al-faras yajūdu jawdatan and jūdatan, with fatḥa or ḍamma; it is a jawād for male and female, and the plural is jiyād, ajwād and ajāwīd; it is also said to be a plural of jawd with fatḥa, like thawb and thiyāb; and it is said to be a plural of jayyid — or from al-jīd, which is the neck, the meaning being "long in the necks", which indicates their excellence.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {حُبَّ الخير}: There are several views on it. First: it is the object (maf'ūl) of «أَحْبَبْت», because that is in the sense of "I preferred" (āthartu), and «عَنْ» on this view means "upon" (ʿalā), i.e. "upon the remembrance of my Lord"; for it is reported in exegesis — and Allah knows best — that he inspected the horses until they distracted him from the afternoon (ʿaṣr) prayer at the beginning of its time, until the sun set. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "It is as if it is transmitted from al-Farrāʾ that he made أَحْبَبْتُ include the sense of آثَرْتُ so that «حُبَّ الخير» is accusative as a direct object. There is some doubt about this, because it is transitive by itself and needs inclusion of another meaning only if it were not transitive." Second: that «حُبَّ» is a maṣdar with the augments removed, governed by «أَحببتُ». Third: that it is a comparative maṣdar, i.e. "a love like the love of good". Fourth: that it is said to include the sense of أَنَبْتُ ("I turned back"), and for that reason it is made transitive with «عن». Fifth: that «أَحْبَبْتُ» means "I held fast to" (lazimtu). Sixth: that «أَحْبَبْتُ» is from aḥabba al-baʿīr, when the camel falls and kneels from exhaustion. The meaning is: "I sat back from the remembrance of my Lord", so «حُبَّ الخيرِ» on this view is a mafʿūl min ajlihi.

His saying: «حتى تَوارَتْ»: As to the agent there are two views. One: it is «الصافنات», the meaning being "until they entered their stables and were hidden and gone". The second: that it is the sun, which is implied because the context indicates it. It is also said: because the evening (al-ʿashiyy) indicates it, as it signals it. And it is said: the shining (al-ishrāq) in the story of David indicates it — how far-fetched!

And his saying: «ذِكْرِ ربي» may be annexed to the object, i.e. "from my remembering my Lord", or annexed to the agent, i.e. "from my Lord's remembering me". The pronoun of the object in «رُدُّوها» refers to «الصافنات». It is also said that it refers to the sun, which is extremely odd.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {مَسْحاً}: Accusative by an implied verb, which is the khabar of «طَفِق», i.e. "he began to wipe, wiping", because the khabar of these verbs is only an imperfect verb in the general rule. Abū al-Baqāʾ said, and he began with it: "A maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl." This is worthless, because «طَفِقَ» must have a khabar.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «مِساحاً» on the pattern of qitāl. The bāʾ in «بالسُّوْق» is redundant, like it in his saying {وامسحوا بِرُؤُوسِكُمْ} [al-Māʾida: 6]. Sībawayh related "masaḥtu raʾsahu and biraʾsihi" with one meaning. It may also be for adhesion (ilṣāq), as its explanation came earlier. The pronouncing of the hamza in al-sūq, or not, was discussed in al-Naml. Al-Fārisī made the hamza weak; but it is not as he said, because of the evidence previously given. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «بالساق» in the singular, being content with the singular where there is no ambiguity, like his saying:

3869 - ... ... and as for its skin, it is hard

and his saying:

3870 - Eat in part of your belly, you will be chaste ... ...

and his saying:

3871 - ... ... in your throat a bone, and we are choked

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: to what is his saying «رُدُّوها عليَّ» connected? I say: to something omitted, whose implied form is: he said, 'Bring them back', so he omitted it and omitted what is its answer. It is as if someone asked: 'What then did Solomon say?', for this is a place that evidently calls for a question." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "This is not needed, because this sentence falls under the reported speech, which is {فَقَالَ إني أَحْبَبْتُ}."

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {جَسَداً}: There are two views on it. The more apparent: that it is a direct object of «أَلْقَيْنا». In the exegesis it is said that it was half of a child. The second: that it is a ḥāl, whose owner is either Solomon — because it is reported that he fell ill until he became like a body without a soul in it — or his child. Abū al-Baqāʾ said both; but a body (jasad) is an inert noun, so it must be interpreted as a derived one, i.e. "weak" or "empty".

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {تَجْرِي}: It may be explicative of his saying «سَخَّرْنا», or a ḥāl from «الريح». The majority read «الريح» in the singular, though the meaning is plural. Al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, Abū Jaʿfar and Qatāda read «الرياح» (plural). «رُخاءً» is a ḥāl from the agent of «تَجْري». Al-rukhāʾ means gentle, derived from rakhāwa (softness). The meaning of that is obedience to his command.

His saying: «حيث» is an adverbial attached to «تَجْري» or to «سَخَّرْنا». And «أصاب» means "he intended", in the dialect of Ḥimyar. It is also said: in the dialect of Hajar. It is reported from two men of the people of the language that they set out to see Ruʾba to ask him about this word. He said to them: "Where are you two headed (tuṣībān)?" So they recognised it and said: "This is what we were seeking." Al-Thaʿlabī cited in support of this:

3872 - He aimed at the answer (aṣāba al-jawāb) but could not ... so he missed the answer at the joint (al-mifṣal)

meaning: he intended the answer. One also says «أَصاب اللَّهُ بك خيراً», i.e. "Allah intended good for you". It is also said: the hamza in «أصاب» is for transitivity, from ṣāba yaṣūbu, meaning "to descend"; the object is omitted, i.e. "he struck his troops", that is, wherever he directed them and made them descend like the descent of rain.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {والشياطين}: Conjoined (nasaq) to «الريحَ». And «كلَّ بنَّاءٍ» is a badal from «الشياطين»; the intensive form is used because it is in the setting of recounting favour.

And «آخرين» is conjoined to «كلَّ», so it falls under the ruling of the badal. The explanation of {مُّقَرَّنِينَ فِي الأصفاد} [Ibrāhīm: 49] came earlier at the end of Sūrat Ibrāhīm.

semin-durr:39-39.t: His saying: {بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ}: There are three views on it. First: that it is attached to «عَطاؤُنا», i.e. "We have given you without reckoning or estimation", which indicates the abundance of the giving. Second: that it is a ḥāl from «عَطاؤنا», i.e. "while it is not reckoned against", because it is so copious that it is hard for accountants to keep count of it. Third: that it is attached to «امْنُنْ» or «أمسِكْ»; and it may be a ḥāl from the agent of both, i.e. "not being called to account for it".

semin-durr:40-40.t: His saying: {وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ}: The majority read it accusative, conjoined to the noun of «إنَّ», which is «لَزُلْفَى». Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it nominative as a mubtadaʾ, its khabar being implied because what precedes indicates it; they pause at «لَزلْفَى» and begin with «حُسْنُ مآب», i.e. "and a goodly return is his also".

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {أَيُّوبَ}: Like his saying {عَبْدَنَا دَاوُودَ} [Ṣād: 17]; the same three views apply to it. And «إذْ نادَى» is a badal al-ishtimāl from it. His saying «أني» is brought as a report of his speech by which he called out; had he not reported it, he would have said "that harm had touched him", since he is third person. The majority read it with fatḥa on the hamza, on the basis that he is the one called with this wording. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read it with kasra (innī), on the implying of "saying", or by treating nidāʾ (calling) as equivalent to saying.

His saying: «بِنُصْبٍ»: The majority read it with ḍamma and sukūn (nuṣb). It is said: it is a plural of naṣab (with two fatḥas), like wathan and wuthn, and asad and usd. It is also said: it is a dialectal variant of naṣab, like rushd and rashad, ḥuzn and ḥazan, ʿudm and ʿadam. Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Ḥafṣ and Nāfiʿ in one transmission read it with two ḍammas (nuṣub), which is a heavier form of nuṣb with ḍamma and sukūn, as al-Zamakhsharī said. There is some remoteness in this, as you know that the requirement of the language is the lightening of fuʿul, as in ʿunuq, not the heavying of fuʿl, as in qufl; there is a disagreement on this. The matter of ʿusr and yusr in al-Baqara has already been discussed. Abū Ḥaywa, Yaʿqūb and Ḥafṣ in one transmission read it with fatḥa and sukūn (naṣb). All are of one meaning: weariness and hardship.

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying: {رَحْمَةً}: And «ذكرى» are both mafʿūl min ajlihi, i.e. "We granted them to him for the sake of Our mercy towards him, and so that those of understanding may take heed from his condition."

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying: {ضِغْثاً}: Al-ḍighth is a small bundle of grass and twigs. It is also said: a large bundle of twigs. In the proverb: «ضِغْثٌ على إبَّالَة» ("a bundle on top of a bundle"), and al-ibbāla is a bundle of firewood. The poet said:

3873 - And heavier for me than a heavy-breathing (mount) that I had tied ... and I threw down a bundle (ḍighth) of perfumed fresh grass (Translator's note: the gloss is tentative.)

The origin of the root indicates the gathering of mixed things. This was discussed earlier in Sūrat Yūsuf, at {أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلاَمٍ} [Yūsuf: 44].

His saying: «ولا تَحْنَثْ»: Al-ḥinth is sin. It is also applied to doing what one swore not to do, or leaving what one swore to do, because the two are generally equivalent in this respect.

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying: {عِبَادَنَآ}: Ibn Kathīr read «عَبْدَنا» in the singular. The others read «عبادَنا» in the plural; the script admits both. As for the reading of Ibn Kathīr, «إبراهيمَ» is a badal or a bayān, or is accusative by an implied "I mean"; and what follows it is conjoined to «عبدَنا» itself, not to Ibrāhīm, since otherwise a plural would have to be substituted for a singular. One might say: since what is meant by «عبدنا» is the class, the substitution of a plural for it is allowed. This is like the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās {وإله أبيك إِبْرَاهِيمَ} in al-Baqara on one of the two views, which has already been discussed. As for the reading of the group, it is clear, since it agrees with the first in being plural.

His saying: «الأَيْدي»: The majority read it with the yāʾ retained; it is the plural of yad, either the bodily limb, with which he alluded to deeds, since most deeds are done by the hand; or it is said that what is meant by al-aydī is the plural of yad meaning "favour". ʿAbd Allāh, al-Ḥasan, ʿĪsā and al-Aʿmash read «الأَيْد» without a yāʾ. It is said: it is the first (i.e. the plural of yad) and the yāʾ was dropped, being content with the kasra in place of it, and because al- alternates with tanwīn, and the yāʾ is dropped with tanwīn, so it was treated with al- as it is with it; but this is very weak. It is also said: al-ayd means strength. However, al-Zamakhsharī said: "Interpreting it as al-ayd from taʾyīd is unsettled and not firm." End of quotation. It seems that it was unsettled for him because of the conjoining of al-abṣār (the sights) to it, which suits al-aydī and not al-ayd from taʾyīd. It may be said: the real limbs are not meant, since everyone has them; rather it is an allusion to righteous action and reflection by insight, and so it is not unsettled then, since actual seeing is not meant. It is as if it were said: "possessors of strength and of reflection with insight." Al-Zamakhsharī had leaned toward something of this before that.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying: {بِخَالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى}: Nāfiʿ and Hishām read «بخالصةِ ذكرَى» as an annexation (iḍāfa). There are several views on it. One: that «خالصة» is annexed to «ذكرَى» for clarification, because al-khāliṣa may be remembrance or other than remembrance, as in his saying {بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ} [al-Naml: 7], because a shihāb may be a firebrand or other than that. Two: that «خالصةً» is a maṣdar meaning ikhlāṣ (sincerity), so it is a maṣdar annexed to its object, the agent being omitted, i.e. "by their having made sincere the remembrance of the Abode, and having forgotten the remembrance of this world in its presence". The maṣdar has come in the form fāʿila, like ʿāfiya; or the meaning is "by Our having made sincere for them the remembrance of the Abode". Three: that it is also a maṣdar, meaning khulūṣ (purity), so it is annexed to its agent, i.e. "by the remembrance of the Abode having become pure for them".

The others read it with tanwīn and without annexation. There are several views on it. One: that it is a maṣdar meaning ikhlāṣ, so «ذكرى» is accusative by it; or meaning khulūṣ, so «ذكرى» is nominative by it, as above; the maṣdar acts when it has tanwīn as it acts when annexed. Or «خالصة» is an active participle in its normal sense, and «ذكرى» is a badal or bayān for it, or accusative by an implied "I mean", or nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ. «الدار» may be an object of «ذكرى», or an adverbial: either by extension, or by removal of the preposition; both mentioned by Abū al-Baqāʾ. When «خالصة» is an adjective, it is an adjective of an omitted noun, i.e. "by means of a pure quality".

semin-durr:48-48.t: And «الأَخْيار» is the plural of khayyir, or khayr, with doubling or lightening, like amwāt, the plural of mayyit or mayt.

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {هذا ذِكْرٌ}: A sentence brought to signal that the story has been completed and another has begun. This is as al-Jāḥiẓ did in his books, saying "This is a chapter", and then beginning another. What indicates this is that when He wished to follow with the mention of the people of the Fire, He mentioned the people of Paradise. The Exalted said: {هذا وَإِنَّ لِلطَّاغِينَ} [Ṣād: 55].

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ}: The majority read «جنات» accusative, as a badal from «حُسْنَ مَآب», whether «جنات عدنٍ» is definite or indefinite, because a definite may be substituted for an indefinite and vice versa. It may also be an ʿaṭf bayān if it is indefinite, but this is not allowed if it is definite. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that after judging and arguing that it is definite; this is like what came earlier from him in several places where he allows ʿaṭf bayān even where the two differ in definiteness and indefiniteness. This was discussed at His saying, the Exalted: {فِيهِ آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ مَّقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 97]. «جناتِ عَدْنٍ» may also be accusative by an implied verb. And «مُفَتَّحةً» is a ḥāl from «جنات عدن», or an adjective of it if it is indefinite. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "A ḥāl, and what governs it is the verbal sense in «للمتقين»." End of quotation. Abū al-Baqāʾ gave a reason in the case of «مُتَّكئين» which would require «مُفَتَّحة» not to be a ḥāl, even though the reason is not sound. He said: "«متكئين» cannot be a ḥāl from «للمتقين», because a predication about them has already been made before the ḥāl." This reason applies equally to making «مُفَتَّحةً» a ḥāl from «للمتقين», as al-Zamakhsharī mentioned. But this reason is not sound; it is comparable to your saying "Hind has wealth, standing". Also, there is looseness in his expression: for «للمتقين» is not predicated of grammatically; it is predicated of in meaning only, otherwise «حُسْن مآب» has been predicated as being theirs. Al-Ḥawfī made the governor an implied one, i.e. "they enter it open".

His saying: «الأبواب»: As to its being nominative there are two views. One — the one well known among people — is that it is nominative by the passive participle, as in His saying {وَفُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُهَا} [al-Zumar: 73]. An objection was raised to this: «مُفتَحةً» is either a ḥāl or an adjective of «جنات», and on either assumption there is no link (rābiṭ). It was answered in two ways. One: the saying of the Basrans, that there is an implied pronoun, the implied form being "the gates of it". The second: that al- stands in place of the pronoun, the original being "its gates"; this is the Kufan view, and its verification came earlier. The two views apply also to His saying {فَإِنَّ الجنة هِيَ المأوى} [al-Nāziʿāt: 41]. The second view: that it is nominative as a badal from the pronoun in «مُفَتَّحَةً» which refers back to «جنات»; this is the saying of al-Fārisī, who, seeing it lacked a link in the wording, claimed this. An objection was raised against it: it would be a badal of part or of inclusion, and both require a pronoun, so one is forced to assume it as before. Some preferred the first view because it has one implied element while this one has two; al-Zamakhsharī followed him and said: "«والأبواب» is a badal from the pronoun in «مُفَتَّحَةً», i.e. 'opened — they, the gates', as you say: Zayd was struck on the hand and the foot; and it is a badal al-ishtimāl." By his saying "badal al-ishtimāl" he only means al-abwāb, since it may be said that the gates are not part of the gardens; whereas "Zayd was struck on the hand and the foot" is a part of a whole and nothing else.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Abū Ḥaywa read {جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ مُّفَتَّحَةٌ} with both nominative: either as one sentence of mubtadaʾ and khabar, or each one is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are gardens; they are opened".

semin-durr:51-51.t: His saying: {مُتَّكِئِينَ}: A ḥāl from «لهم»; what governs it is «مفتحةً». It is also said: what governs it is «تُوْعَدون», which has been delayed after it. Abū al-Baqāʾ's prohibition of its being a ḥāl from «للمتقين», and what is in that, has already been discussed. And «يَدْعُون» may be resumptive, or a ḥāl: either from the pronoun of «مُتَّكئين», or a second ḥāl.

semin-durr:53-53.t: His saying: {تُوعَدُونَ}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read here «يُوْعَدون» in the third person. In Sūrat Qāf, Ibn Kathīr alone does. The others read the second person in both. The reason for the third person here and in Qāf is the preceding mention of the God-fearing. The reason for the second person is the turning (iltifāt) toward them and addressing them directly.

semin-durr:54-54.t: His saying: {مَا لَهُ مِن نَّفَادٍ}: «مِنْ نَفادٍ» is either a mubtadaʾ or an agent, and «مِنْ» is redundant. The sentence is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from «رزقنا», i.e. "not perishing". It may also be a second khabar.

semin-durr:55-55.t: His saying: {هذا وَإِنَّ لِلطَّاغِينَ}: «هذا» may be a mubtadaʾ with an implied khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī implied: "This is as mentioned"; Abū ʿAlī implied: "This is for the believers". It may also be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is this".

semin-durr:56-56.t: His saying: {جَهَنَّمَ}: It may be a badal from «شرَّ مآبٍ» or accusative by an implied verb. By the analogy of al-Zamakhsharī's statement on «جناتِ عدن», it may be an ʿaṭf bayān, and it may be accusative by an implied verb in the manner of ishtighāl, i.e. "they will burn in Jahannam, they will burn in it". The makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm (the specified subject of censure) is omitted, i.e. "it".

semin-durr:57-57.t:
His saying: {هذا فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ}: There are several views on «هذا». One: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «حميمٌ وغَسَّاقٌ». It was mentioned earlier that a demonstrative may be satisfied with its singular form for the dual, as in His saying {عَوَانٌ بَيْنَ ذلك} [al-Baqara: 68]; or the meaning is "this combines the two descriptions", and His saying «فَلْيَذُوْقوه» is then a parenthetical sentence. Two: that «هذا» is accusative by an implied verb in the manner of ishtighāl, i.e. "let them taste this". Al-Zamakhsharī likened it to His saying, the Exalted, {وَإِيَّايَ فارهبون} [al-Baqara: 40], meaning in the manner of ishtighāl. Discussion of this kind of point has been given earlier. «حميمٌ» on this view is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, or a mubtadaʾ with an implied khabar, i.e. "of it is boiling water and of it is ghassāq", as in his saying:

3874 - Until, when the lightning flashed in the pre-dawn darkness ... and the herbage was left twisted and reaped

i.e. "some of it twisted and some of it reaped". Three: that «هذا» is a mubtadaʾ with an omitted khabar, i.e. "this is as mentioned", or "this is for the transgressors". Four: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is this", then He began a new command and said: let them taste it. Five: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «فَلْيذوقوه»; this is the opinion of al-Akhfash. Of this is:

3875 - And many a woman says: "Khawlān! — marry their girl ..." ... (Translator's note: the verse is incomplete in the source.)

The verification of this came earlier in al-Māʾida at {والسارق والسارقة} [al-Māʾida: 38]. Al-Kisāʾī, Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ read «غَسَّاقٌ» with doubled sīn here and in ʿamma yatasāʾalūn; the others lightened it in both. As for the doubled form, it is an adjective, like jabbār and ḍarrāb, an intensive pattern, since faʿʿāl is more frequent in adjectives than in nouns. Among its occurrences in nouns are: al-kallāʾ, al-jabbān, and al-fayyād for the male owl, al-ʿaqqār and al-khaṭṭār. As for the lightened form, it is a noun and not an adjective, because faʿāl with lightening is more frequent in nouns, like ʿadhāb and nakāl, than in adjectives; although some made it an adjective meaning "possessor of such", i.e. "possessor of ghasaq". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "or faʿʿāl is in the sense of fāʿil." I say: this is not known. Al-Ghasaq is flowing. One says ghasaqat ʿaynuhu, i.e. "his eye flowed". In the exegesis: it is a water flowing from their pus. It is also said: ghasaqa means "it was filled"; of it is ghasaqat ʿaynuhu, "his eye filled with tears", and of it al-ghāsiq for the moon, for its fullness and completeness. It is also said: al-ghassāq is what kills by its cold; of it the night is called ghāsiq, since it is colder than the day. It is also said: al-ghasaq is intensity of darkness, and of it the night is called "ghāsiq". The moon is also called ghāsiq when it is eclipsed, for its blackening. The two views are transmitted in the exegesis of His saying, the Exalted: {وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ} [al-Falaq: 3].

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {وَآخَرُ}: Abū ʿAmr read it with ḍamma on the hamza (ukharu), as a plural. Its being nominative is explained in several ways. One: that it is a mubtadaʾ, «من شَكْلِه» its khabar, and «أزواجٌ» an agent of it. Two: that it is also a mubtadaʾ, «مِنْ شكلِه» a fronted khabar, and «أزواج» a mubtadaʾ whose sentence is the khabar. On both of these it is asked: how can it be sound without a pronoun returning to ukhar, since the pronoun in «شكله» refers to what came before, i.e. "of the kind of what is tasted"? The answer: the pronoun refers to the mubtadaʾ, and it is put in the singular masculine only because the meaning is "of the kind of what we have mentioned". Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this interpretation. Makkī forbade that, because of the absence of the pronoun; the answer is what I have mentioned to you. Three: that «مِنْ شكله» is an adjective of ukhar, and azwāj is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and others, of the kind of what is tasted, are pairs". Four: that «من شكله» is also an adjective, azwāj is an agent of it, and the pronoun refers to ukhar by the interpretation given above; on this ukharu is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is implied, i.e. "and they will have other kinds, of whose like pairs are established". Five: that the khabar is implied as before, i.e. "and they will have others", and «ومِنْ شكلِه» and «أزواج» are two adjectives of ukhar.

The majority read «مِنْ شَكْلِه» with fatḥa on the shīn; Mujāhid read it with kasra (shikl); they are two dialects meaning "the like" and "the kind". You say: "this is of his shakl", i.e. his like and kind. As for shikl meaning coquetry (ghunj), it is with kasra only, said al-Zamakhsharī.

The others read «وآخَرُ» with fatḥa on the hamza followed by an alif, in the form of the elative afʿal; the grammatical analysis of it is as above. In one of the views, the pronoun refers to it without interpretation, because it is singular. However, in one of the views it follows that a singular is predicated of by a plural, or a singular is described by a plural, because among the views above is that «أزواج» is a khabar of «آخر» or an adjective of it. There are two answers to this. One: the implied form is "and another punishment, or another thing tasted, which is of kinds and degrees", so it is equivalent in force to a plural. Or each part of that other is made like the whole and named by its name, which is common and frequent, as in "thick eyebrows" and "his temples grew grey". Moreover, one might say that «أزواج» is an adjective of the three preceding things — I mean the boiling water, the ghassāq and the other of its kind — in which case the question falls away.

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying: {مُّقْتَحِمٌ}: Its object is omitted, i.e. "plunging into the Fire". Iqtiḥām is entering into something with violence; al-quḥma is violence. Al-Rāghib said: "Iqtiḥām is going into the midst of a frightening difficulty. Of it is qaḥama al-faras fārisahu, i.e. the horse plunged with its rider into what is feared. And al-maqāḥīm are those who plunge into the matter that should be avoided."

His saying: «معكم»: It may be a second adjective of fawj, or a ḥāl from it because it has been described, or a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «مُقْتَحِم». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It cannot be an adverbial because the meaning would be spoiled." I do not know in what respects it would be spoiled, given that the ḥāl and the adjective are in meaning like the adverbial.

His saying «هذا فَوْجٌ» to His saying «النار» may be the speech of the chiefs to one another, or the speech of the keepers (of the Fire). It may also be that «هذا فَوْجٌ» is the speech of the angels and the rest the speech of the chiefs. The analogy on this would require saying: "Rather, they — no welcome to them", because they would not say that to the angels; but they turned from addressing the angels to addressing their enemies, to vent their feelings against them.

His saying: {لاَ مَرْحَباً}: There are two views on «مَرْحباً». The more apparent: that it is an object of an implied verb, i.e. "you have not come to a welcome" or "you have not heard a welcome". The second: that it is accusative as a maṣdar, said Abū al-Baqāʾ, i.e. "may your abode not be spacious for you, but narrow". Then there are two views on the negated sentence. One: that it is resumptive, brought as an imprecation against them, and His saying «بهم» is a clarification of those against whom it is invoked. The second: that it is a ḥāl. It may be objected to that: it is a supplication, and a supplication is a request, and a request cannot occur as a ḥāl. The answer: it is on the implying of "saying", i.e. "said to them: no welcome".

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying: {مَن قَدَّمَ}: «مَنْ» may be conditional with «فَزِدْه» as its apodosis; or interrogative, with «قَدَّم» its khabar, i.e. "which person brought this on us?", after which they began an imprecation with their saying «فَزِدْه»; or a relative noun meaning "the one who", in which case there are two views: nominative as mubtadaʾ, with «فَزِدْه» as the khabar and the fāʾ redundant, in likeness to the condition; and second, that it is accusative by an implied verb in the manner of ishtighāl. Discussion of such a fāʾ came earlier. This last view is allowed by some even when it is conditional or interrogative, I mean ishtighāl, except that the verb is not implied except after it, since it has the first place in the sentence. And «ضِعْفاً» is an adjective of «عذاب», i.e. "doubled".

His saying: «في النارِ»: It may be an adverbial attached to «زِدْه», or an adjective of «عذاب», or a ḥāl from it because of its specification, or a ḥāl from the object of «زِدْه».

semin-durr:63-63.t:
His saying: {أَتَّخَذْنَاهُمْ}: Al-Kisāʾī, Ḥamza and Abū ʿAmr read it with a conjunctive hamza (ittakhadhnāhum), which admits two views. One: that it is pure statement, the sentence being in the position of accusative as a second adjective of «رِجالاً», as «كنا نَعُدُّهم» occurred as an adjective; the other: that interrogation is meant and its particle has been omitted because «أم» indicates it, as in his saying:

3876 - Are you departing from the tribe, or will you leave early? ... What harm would it do you if you waited?

So «أم» is connected (muttaṣila) on this view, whereas on the first it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning "rather" and the hamza, since no interrogative or equalising hamza precedes it. The others read with an interrogative hamza, for which the conjunctive hamza dropped. Apparently the sentence then has no grammatical position because it is a request-type sentence. Some allowed that it be an adjective but on the implying of "saying", i.e. "men about whom it was said: did we take them...", as in his saying:

3877 - They brought diluted milk: "Have you ever seen the wolf ...?" (Translator's note: the verse is incomplete in the source.)

except that the adjective in reality is that implied saying. The disagreement over «سِخْرِيَّاً» was discussed earlier at {قَدْ أَفْلَحَ المؤمنون}. The well-known view is that the form with kasra is for mockery, as in the poet's saying:

3778 - A tongue has reached me, which I am not pleased by ... from on high, with no lie in it and no mockery (sakhr) (Translator's note: the source prints the number as 3778; from the sequence it should evidently be 3878.)

The meaning of the attachment of the doubled yāʾ in that was discussed earlier. «أم» with a statement is only disconnected, as above; with an interrogative it may be connected or disconnected, as in your saying "Is Zayd with you, or is ʿAmr with you?". It may be that «أم زاغَتْ» is connected to His saying «ما لنا», since it is an interrogative, except that its being disconnected is required because of the absence of the hamza; and what is between them would be parenthetical on the reading «أتَّخَذْناهم» with interrogation, if we do not make it an adjective on the implying of "saying", as above.

semin-durr:64-64.t:
His saying: {تَخَاصُمُ}: The majority read «تَخاصُمُ» nominative, annexed to «أهل». There are several views on it. One: that it is a badal from «لَحَقٌّ». Two: that it is an ʿaṭf bayān. Three: that it is a badal from «ذلك» in position, related by Makkī; this agrees with the saying of some Kufans. Four: that it is a second khabar of «إنَّ». Five: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is the disputing". Six: that it is nominative by His saying «لَحَقٌّ». However, Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Were it said that it is nominative by «حَقٌّ», it would be remote, because it would become a sentence in which no pronoun returns to the noun of «إن»." This is a sound refutation. It may be answered: the pronoun is implied, i.e. "the disputing of the people of the Fire about it is true", as in His saying {وَلَمَن صَبَرَ وَغَفَرَ إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَمِنْ عَزْمِ الأمور} [al-Shūrā: 43], i.e. "from it". Ibn Muḥayṣin read «تخاصمٌ» with tanwīn and «أهلُ» nominative: «تخاصمٌ» is nominative as above; as for the nominative «أهلُ», it is as agent of the maṣdar with tanwīn, as in your saying "The disputing of the Zaydites pleases me", i.e. that they dispute. This is the view of the Basrans and some Kufans except al-Farrāʾ.

Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «تخاصمَ» accusative, annexed to «أهل». There are several views on it. One: that it is an adjective of «ذلك» in wording. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because demonstratives are described by generic nouns." There is some doubt about this, because they stated explicitly that demonstratives are described only by what has al-, as in "O this man", and "O this boy of the man" is not allowed; so this is more remote. Also, the correct view is that what falls after a demonstrative accompanied by al-, if derived, is an adjective, and otherwise a badal, and «تخاصم» is not derived. Two: that it is a badal from «ذلك». Three: that it is an ʿaṭf bayān. Four: on the implying of "I mean". Abū al-Faḍl said: "Were «تخاصم» made accusative as a badal from «ذلك», it would be allowed." End of quotation. It seems that he did not come across it as a reading. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «تخاصَمَ» as a past verb, with «أهل» as its agent. It is a resumptive sentence.

semin-durr:65-65.t: His saying: {الواحد القهار}: To the end of it, these are attributes of Allah, the Exalted. «ربُّ السماواتِ» may be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, with the sense of praise in it.

semin-durr:67-67.t: His saying: {هُوَ نَبَأٌ}: «هو» refers to the Qur'an and the stories and reports in it. It is also said: to {تَخَاصُمُ أَهْلِ النار}. And it is said: to what came earlier of his reports, peace be upon him — that he is a clear warner, and that Allah is one God, characterised by those most beautiful attributes.

semin-durr:68-68.t: His saying: {أَنتُمْ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضُونَ}: An adjective of «نَبَأ», or resumptive.

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His saying: {بالملإ}: Attached to His saying «مِنْ عِلْم»; it includes the sense of encompassing, and for that reason it is made transitive with the bāʾ. Its verification came earlier.

And His saying: «إذ يَخْتَصِمُون»: There are two views on it. One: that it is accusative by the maṣdar as well. The second: by an implied muḍāf, i.e. "of the speech of the Highest Assembly when", said al-Zamakhsharī. The pronoun in «يَخْتَصِمُون» refers to the Highest Assembly; this is the apparent view. It is also said: to Quraysh, i.e. "they dispute about the Highest Assembly", some saying "daughters of Allah" and others saying otherwise. The implied form is then: "when they dispute about them".

semin-durr:70-70.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ أَنَّمَآ أَنَاْ}: The majority read «أنما» with fatḥa on the hamza. There are two views on it. One: that it, together with what follows it, is in the position of nominative, standing in place of the agent (i.e. as nāʾib fāʿil), i.e. "nothing is revealed to me except the warning", or "except my being a clear warner". The second: that it is in the position of accusative or genitive after the dropping of the lām of cause. The deputy agent on this view is the preposition and its genitive noun, i.e. "nothing is revealed to me except for the warning" or "for my being a warner". On this view the deputy agent may also be a pronoun for something the context indicates, i.e. "that thing is not revealed to me except for the warning".

Abū Jaʿfar read it with kasra (innamā), which is the deputy agent by way of quotation, as if it were said: "nothing is revealed to me except this sentence, which contains this report." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "by way of quotation, i.e. except this saying, which is that I say to you: I am only a clear warner, and I claim nothing else." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "There is a conflict in his explanation, because he said 'except this saying', whose apparent sense is the sentence {أَنَّمَآ أَنَاْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ}; then he said 'which is that I say to you that I am a warner', so the deputy agent is 'that I say to you', and «إنِّي» and what follows is in the position of accusative; whereas by his saying 'except this saying' it would be in the position of nominative; so they conflict." I say: there is no conflict at all, because the second is an explanation of meaning and the first an explanation of grammatical analysis, so there is no conflict.

semin-durr:71-71.t:
His saying: {إِذْ قَالَ}: It may be a badal from the first «إذ», or accusative by an implied "remember". Al-Zamakhsharī stated the first without qualification, and Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned the second without qualification. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān), however, differentiated and said: "A badal from «إذ يَخْتصمون». This holds if the dispute concerned who would be made a successor on the earth; according to other views it is accusative by «اذكرْ»." End of quotation. I say: those views are that the disputing was either among the Highest Assembly or among Quraysh, and over what the dispute was is a disagreement whose mention would lengthen the book.

His saying: «مِنْ طينٍ»: It may be attached to an omitted adjective of «بَشَراً», or attached to «خالِقٌ» itself.

semin-durr:73-73.t: His saying: {كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ}: Two emphases (tawkīd). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«كل» is for encompassing and «أجمعون» for togetherness, so together they convey that they prostrated to the last of them, no angel remaining that did not prostrate, and that they prostrated all together at one time, not separately." I say: the discussion with him on this came earlier in Sūrat al-Ḥijr.

semin-durr:75-75.t:
His saying: {أَن تَسْجُدَ}: One who holds that «لا» in {أَلاَّ تَسْجُدَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 12] in the other sūra is redundant may cite this as evidence, since it is absent here though the story is one. And His saying «لما خَلَقْتُ»: one who holds that «ما» may be used for a rational being may cite it as evidence, since Adam is meant. It is also said: there is no evidence in it, because he was then moulded clay, not a sentient body, so he was referred to in that state. And it is said: «ما» is maṣdarī and the maṣdar is not meant, so it stands in the place of the object, i.e. "to My creature".

Al-Jaḥdarī read «لَمَّا» with doubled mīm and fatḥa on the lām, which is the temporal lammā according to al-Fārisī, and a particle of the occurrence of one thing due to the occurrence of another according to Sībawayh. The one to be prostrated to on this reading is not mentioned, i.e. "What prevented you from prostrating when I created — that is, when I created — the one I commanded you to prostrate to?" It was also read «بيَدَيِّ» with kasra on the yāʾ, like Ḥamza's reading «بِمُصْرِخِيِّ», whose discussion came earlier. And «بيدي» was read in the singular.

His saying: «أسْتَكْبَرْت»: The majority read it with an interrogative hamza, an interrogation of rebuke and denial, and «أم» here is connected. This is the saying of the majority of grammarians. Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted from some grammarians that it is not the counterpart of the alif when the two verbs differ, and is a counterpart only when they enter upon a single verb, as in your saying "Did Zayd stand, or ʿAmr?" and "Did Zayd stand, or ʿAmr?" [sic]; and when the verbs differ, as in this verse, it is not a counterpart. What he transmitted from some grammarians is a corrupt doctrine; rather, the majority of grammarians are against it. Sībawayh said: "You say: 'Did you strike Zayd or kill him?' Beginning here with the verb is better, because you are asking about one of the two without knowing which it was, and you are not asking about the place of one of them, as if you said: which of these was it?" End of quotation. So he made it the counterpart of the alif although the two verbs differ.

A group — among them Ibn Kathīr, though it is not well known from him — read «استكبَرْتَ» with a conjunctive alif, which admits two views. One: that interrogation is intended, indicated by «أم», as in his saying:

3879 - ... ... with seven they threw the pebbles, or with eight

and the other's saying:

3880 - Are you departing from the tribe, or will you leave early? ... ...

so the two readings agree in meaning. It also admits being pure statement, in which case «أم» is disconnected, because its condition is absent.

semin-durr:77-77.t: His saying: {مِنْهَا}: i.e. from Paradise, or from the (angelic) form, because he had been beautiful and returned ugly, luminous and returned dark. It is also said: from the heavens. He said here «لَعْنتي» and elsewhere «اللعنةَ»; though in wording one is general and the other specific, in meaning both are general by implication, because whoever is under the curse of Allah is inevitably under the curse of everyone. The Exalted said: {أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةُ الله والملائكة والناس أَجْمَعِينَ} [al-Baqara: 161]. The remaining sentences have parallels already discussed.

semin-durr:84-84.t:
His saying: {فالحق والحق}: The majority read both accusative. As to the accusative of the first there are several views. One: that it is what is sworn by, from which the particle of oath was dropped so it became accusative, as in his saying:

3881 - ... ... that, by the trust of Allah (amānata Allāh), is the tharīd (bread-and-meat dish)

semin-durr:85-85.t:
And His saying: {لأَمْلأَنَّ}: The answer to the oath. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Except that Sībawayh rejects it, since he does not allow the dropping of the particle of oath except with the name of Allah, and «والحقَّ أقول» would be parenthetical between the oath and its answer." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is as if it were said: 'and I say only the truth'", meaning that fronting the object conveyed restriction. What is meant by al-ḥaqq is either the Creator, the Exalted, as in His saying {وَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ الله هُوَ الحق المبين} [al-Nūr: 25], or the opposite of falsehood. The second view: that it is accusative as incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. "hold fast to the truth". The third: that it is a confirmatory maṣdar for the content of His saying «لأَمْلأَنَّ». Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is in the sense of your saying 'truly, no doubt'; and the presence of al- and its omission are the same, i.e. 'I will surely fill Hell, truly'." End of quotation. This does not work on the Basran view: for the condition of accusative of a confirmatory maṣdar for the content of a sentence is that it come after a nominal sentence whose mubtadaʾ and khabar are both definite and purely inert nouns. Ibn al-ʿIlj allowed the khabar to be indefinite. Furthermore, a confirmatory maṣdar may not precede the sentence whose content it confirms; this was discussed earlier. As for the second, it is accusative by «أقولُ» after it, and the sentence is parenthetical, as above. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be accusative as repetition (takrīr), meaning that the first and the second are both accusative by أقولُ. The clarification of that will come in his wording.

ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read the first nominative and the second accusative. The first's being nominative is explained in several ways. One: that it is a mubtadaʾ with an implied khabar, the implied form being "so the truth is from Me" or "so the truth is I". Two: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «لأملأنَّ», said Ibn ʿAṭiyya. He said: "because the meaning is: 'that I fill'." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "This is nothing, because «لأملأنَّ» is the answer to an oath and must be a sentence, so it cannot be construed as a single word. Also it is not a maṣdar implied by a maṣdar-forming particle and the verb, so as to resolve into them; but since it was possible to attribute what he implied to the mubtadaʾ, he judged that it is a khabar of it." I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya's interpretation is sound in meaning, though not in the technical analysis.

Three: that it is a mubtadaʾ with an implied khabar, the implied form being "so the truth is my oath", and «لأملأنَّ» is the answer to the oath, as in His saying {لَعَمْرُكَ إِنَّهُمْ لَفِي سَكْرَتِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ} [al-Ḥijr: 72]; but omitting the khabar here is not obligatory, since it is not explicit in oath, unlike لَعَمْرك. Similar is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

3882 - I said: "By the oath of Allah (yamīnu Allāh), I will not cease sitting ... even if they cut off my head and my limbs in your presence"

As for the accusative of the second, it is by the verb after it. Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and al-Aʿmash read both nominative. The first's nominative is as above, and the second's nominative is as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the sentence after it, the returning pronoun omitted, as in His saying, the Exalted, in the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir: {وَكُلٌ وَعَدَ الله الحسنى} and the saying of Abū al-Najm:

3883 - Umm al-Khiyār has taken to claiming against me ... a sin, all of which I did not commit

It may also be nominative by repetition according to al-Zamakhsharī, as will come. Al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā read both genitive. Its explanation: the first is genitive by an implied wāw of oath, i.e. "so by the truth", and «والحقِ» is conjoined to it, as in your saying "By Allah, by Allah, I will surely stand", and «أقول» is parenthetical between the oath and its answer. It may also be genitive by way of quotation, while being in the position of accusative by «أقولُ» after it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And both genitive — i.e. they were read as genitives — on the basis that the first is what is sworn by, its particle of oath implied, as you say 'Allah, I will surely do', and «والحقَّ أقول», i.e. 'I say only the truth', by quoting the wording of what is sworn by; its meaning is emphasis and intensification. This view is also allowed for the nominative and accusative, and it is a fine, subtle view." End of quotation. He means that he made «أقول» govern «والحق» by way of quotation, so it is accusative by «أقول» whether it is accusative, nominative or genitive, as if it were said: "and I say this preceding expression, bound by what was uttered first."

His saying: «أجمعين»: There are two views on it. The more apparent: that it is an emphasis of the pronoun in «منك», and «لمَنْ» is conjoined in His saying «ومِمَّنْ تَبِعك», and «أجمعين» was used rather than «كل», though it was mentioned earlier that the more frequent usage is the opposite. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it be an emphasis of the pronoun in «منهم» in particular, so he implied: "I will surely fill Hell with the devils and with those of all mankind who follow them, no difference in that between one people and another."

semin-durr:86-86.t: His saying: {عَلَيْهِ}: Attached to «أسْألكم», not to «الأَجْر», because it is a maṣdar; it may also be a ḥāl from it. The pronoun refers either to the Qur'an, to the revelation, or to the call to Allah. And «لتعلمُنَّ» is the answer to an implied oath, whose meaning is: "and you will surely know."

semin-durr:1-1.t:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
The majority read «صادْ» with sukūn on the dāl, like the rest of the disconnected letters at the beginnings of the sūras. What is in it has preceded. Ubayy, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Abū al-Sammāl read with kasra on the dāl without tanwīn. There are two views on it. One: it is a kasra because of the meeting of two sukūns, and this is nearer. The second: it is an imperative from muṣādāt, which is counter-matching (muʿāraḍa); from it comes the sound of the echo (ṣadā), because of its matching your voice, and that in hard, empty places. The meaning: "match the Qur'an with your deed, so act by its commands and refrain from its prohibitions." Al-Ḥasan said it. It is also reported from him that it is from ṣādaytu, that is: ḥādathtu (I conversed). The meaning: "converse with people by the Qur'an."
Ibn Abī Isḥāq read likewise, except that he added tanwīn, on the basis that it is genitive by an implied oath particle, which was omitted while its effect remained, like their saying «اللَّهِ لأفعلَنَّ» with genitive. However, the genitive is rare with other than the Name of Majesty; he made it triptote only by taking it to the meaning of "the Book" and "the revelation." Also from al-Ḥasan, Ibn al-Samayfaʿ and Hārūn al-Aʿwar: «صادُ» with ḍamma without tanwīn, on the basis that it is a name of the sūra, and it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "this is Ṣād." It is barred from tanwīn for being a proper name and feminine. Likewise Ibn al-Samayfaʿ and Hārūn read «قاف» and «نون» with ḍamma, as preceded.
ʿĪsā and Abū ʿAmr, in the transmission of Maḥbūb, read «صادَ» with fatḥa without tanwīn. It has three possibilities: being indeclinable on fatḥa for lightness, like ayna and kayfa; the genitive by an implied oath particle, being barred from tanwīn for being a proper name and feminine, as preceded; and the accusative by an implied verb or by omission of the oath particle, as in the saying:
3829 - ... so that, by the trust of Allah, is the tharīd [the dish]
It is barred from tanwīn for the reason given. Likewise they read «قاف» and «نون» with fatḥa in both, and they are as preceded; I have not memorised tanwīn with fatḥa or ḍamma.
His saying: «والقرآنِ»: its like has preceded in {يس والقرآن} [Yā Sīn: 1-2]. The answer to the oath has many views. One: that it is His saying {إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ} [Ṣād: 64]; al-Zajjāj and the Kufans other than al-Farrāʾ said it. Al-Farrāʾ said: "We do not find it sound, because it is very far from His saying «والقرآن»." The second: that it is His saying «كم أهلَكْنا»; the original is «لكم أهلَكْنا», and he omitted the lām as he omitted it in His saying {قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّاهَا} [al-Shams: 9] after His saying {والشمس}, when the speech became long. Thaʿlab and al-Farrāʾ said it. The third: that it is His saying {إِن كُلٌّ إِلاَّ كَذَّبَ الرسل} [Ṣād: 14]; al-Akhfash said it. The fourth: that it is His saying «صاد», because the meaning is "By the Qur'an, Muḥammad has spoken truly." Al-Farrāʾ and Thaʿlab also said it. This is a construction on their part on the permissibility of fronting the answer to the oath, and that this letter is cut off from a sentence which it indicates. Both are weak. The fifth: that it is omitted. They disagreed on its estimation. Al-Ḥūfī said: / its estimation is "the truth has come to you," and the like. Ibn ʿAṭiyya estimated: "the matter is not as they claim." Al-Zamakhsharī: "it is miraculous (inna-hu la-muʿjiz)." And the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān]: "you are among the messengers (innaka la-min al-mursalīn)." He said: "because it is the parallel of {يس * والقرآن الحكيم * إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ المرسلين} [Yā Sīn: 1-3]." Al-Zamakhsharī has here an extremely ugly expression. It is: "If you say: His saying «ص والقرآنِ ذي الذكر بل الذين كفروا في عِزَّةٍ وشِقاقٍ» is a speech whose apparent sense is self-contradictory and unstructured, what is the way of its structure? I say: there are two ways. That He mentioned the name of this letter of the alphabet by way of challenge and a pointer to inimitability, as passed at the beginning of the Book, then followed it with the oath with its answer omitted because the challenge indicates it, as if He said: 'By the Qur'an possessing the Reminder, it is an inimitable speech.' The second: that «صاد» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, on the basis that it is a name of the sūra, as if He said: 'This is Ṣād,' meaning this sūra that rendered the Arabs incapable, 'and by the Qur'an possessing the Reminder,' as you say 'This is Ḥātim, by Allah,' meaning: he is the one famed for generosity, by Allah; and likewise when He swears by it, as if He said: 'I swear by Ṣād and by the Qur'an possessing the Reminder that it is inimitable.' Then He said: 'Nay, those who disbelieve are in pride and arrogance against submitting to that and acknowledging it, and in opposition to Allah and His Messenger.' And if you make it that sworn by, and conjoin to it {والقرآن ذِي الذكر}, it is permissible for you to mean by 'the Qur'an' the whole revelation, and to mean the particular sūra. Its meaning: 'I swear by the noble sūra, and by the Qur'an possessing the Reminder,' as you say: 'I passed by the generous man and the blessed soul (nasama),' not meaning by 'nasama' other than the man.'"

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {بَلِ الذين كَفَرُواْ}: an iḍrāb (turning away) of transition from one story to another. Al-Kisāʾī in the transmission of Sawra, Ḥammād ibn al-Zibriqān, Abū Jaʿfar and al-Jaḥdarī read «في غِرَّةٍ» with a dotted ghayn and rāʾ. It has been reported that Ḥammād the transmitter read it so by misreading, and when it was rejected to him he said: "I did not think the disbelievers were in ʿizza." This is a delusion of his, because the ʿizza referred to is the zeal of pre-Islamic ignorance. The indefiniteness in «عزَّة وشِقاق» indicates their intensity and aggravation.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {أن جاءكم}: that is: "min an" ("because"), and there is the well-known disagreement about it.
And His saying: «وقال الكافرون» is of the category of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, as a testimony against them with this ugly description.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {عُجَابٌ}: an intensive of «عجيب», as they say rajul ṭuwāl and amr surāʿ; both are more intensive than ṭawīl and sarīʿ. ʿAlī, al-Sulamī, ʿĪsā and Ibn Miqsam read «عُجَّاب» with tashdīd on the jīm, which is more intensive than the former, so it is like rajul karīm, kurām with light and kurrām with tashdīd. Muqātil said: "ʿujāb, meaning the light one, is the dialect of Azd Shanūʾa." This reading, I mean with tashdīd, is like His saying {وَمَكَرُواْ مَكْراً كُبَّاراً} [Nūḥ: 22]; it is more intensive than kubār, and kubār is more intensive than kabīr.
And His saying: «أجَعَلَ», that is: "Did he turn them into one god," in his saying and his claim.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {أَنِ امشوا}: «أنْ» may be maṣdarī, that is: "they went off with their saying: 'Walk!'"; and it may be explicative (mufassira): either of «انطلق», because it was made to include the meaning of saying. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "because those who go off from a meeting of dispute / must speak and exchange views about what happened to them." End. It was also said: rather it explains an omitted sentence in the position of a ḥāl, its estimation: "and they went off conversing, saying 'Walk!'" It may be maṣdarī, governed by this omitted element. It was also said: al-inṭilāq here is the rush into saying and speech, as in inṭalaqa lisānuhu, so «أنْ» explains it without inclusion or omission. As for al-mashy, the apparent is that it is the well-known one. It was also said: rather it is a prayer for abundance of livestock; this is invalid in wording and meaning. As for the wording, from this meaning one says only amshā l-rajulu, with alif, when his livestock became abundant, that is: he became an owner of livestock; so on this it should have been read «أَمْشُوا» with a hamzat qaṭʿ with fatḥa. As for the meaning, it is not intended at all, and what meaning is there in that!
However, al-Zamakhsharī mentioned a view that is sound in terms of the craft and nearer in meaning than the preceding, saying: "It is possible that they said: 'imshū,' that is: 'multiply and gather,' from mashat al-marʾa, when her childbearing became abundant; from it comes al-māshiya, as a good omen." End. And if one stops at «أنْ» and begins with what follows it, one should begin with kasra on the hamza, not with ḍamma, because the third letter is with kasra by estimation, as the original is imshiyū, and then it was altered by omission. This is like beginning with ḍamma on the hamza in your saying «اغْزِي يا امرأةُ» (O woman, raid!), even though the zāy is with kasra, because it is with ḍamma in the original, the original being ighzuwī like ukhrujī, and it was altered by omission.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {فِى الملة}: there are two views on it. One: that it is attached to «سَمِعْنا», that is: "we have not heard in the latter religion of this that you have brought." The second: that it is attached to an omitted element, as a ḥāl from «هذا», that is: "we have not heard of this, as existing in the latter religion," that is: we did not hear from the soothsayers nor from the People of the Books that the oneness of Allah would arise in the latter religion; and this is of the extremity of their lying.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {أَأُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ الذكر}: the ruling on these two hamzas has preceded at the beginning of Āl ʿImrān, and the fact that what occurs of it in the Qur'an is in three places. The iḍrābs (turnings) in this verse are clear, and «أم» is munqaṭiʿa (disconnected).

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {فَلْيَرْتَقُواْ}: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "This is a speech construed on the meaning, that is: 'if they claim that, let them ascend.'" So he made it the apodosis of an implied condition, and al-Zamakhsharī often does that.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {جُندٌ}: two views are permissible in it. One, and it is the apparent: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "they are a host." And «ما» has two views: one, that it is redundant; the second, that it is an adjective of «جُنْدٌ», by way of magnification, or to mock them, or for belittlement, for the descriptive «ما» is used for these two meanings. Like it is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
3850 - ... and a talk, whatever, for all its brevity
This has already preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. And «هنالك» has three views: one, that it is the khabar of «الجند», «ما» is redundant and «مَهْزُوم» is an adjective of «جُنْد»; Makkī mentioned it. The second: that it is an adjective of «جند». The third: that it is accusative by «مهزوم». And «مهزوم» also has two views: one, that it is a second khabar of that implied mubtadaʾ; the second, that it is an adjective of «جُنْد», except that on this view it is better not to make «هنالك» an adjective but attached to it, so as not to require that a non-explicit description precede an explicit one. «هنالك» points to the place of the dispute and the passing over of the preceding words, which is Mecca, that is: "they will be routed in Mecca," and this is a report of the unseen. It was also said: it points to the support of the idols. It was also said: to the digging of the trench, meaning: to the place of that. The second of the first two views: that «جندٌ» is a mubtadaʾ and «ما» redundant, «هنالك» an adjective and «مهزوم» its khabar; Abū al-Baqāʾ said it. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "There is remoteness in it because of its breaking away from the preceding speech."
I say: this view reported from Abū al-Baqāʾ was preceded by Makkī.
His saying: «من الأحزاب»: it may be an adjective of «جُند» and it may be an adjective of «مهزومٌ». Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted that it be attached to it. There is remoteness in it, because what is meant by al-aḥzāb are the routed ones themselves.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {ذُو الأوتاد}: this is an eloquent metaphor, in that he likened sovereignty to a hair tent (bayt al-shaʿr), and the hair tent holds only by pegs and ropes, as al-Afwah said:
3851 - The tent is built only on posts, and there are no posts unless pegs are fixed
So it is borrowed for the firmness of might and sovereignty and the settledness of the affair, as in the saying of al-Aswad:
3852 - ... in the shade of a kingdom firm of pegs
/ Al-awtād is the plural of watid. It has dialects: watid with fatḥa on the wāw and kasra on the tāʾ, which is the most eloquent; watad with two fatḥas; and wadd with assimilation of the tāʾ into the dāl. He said: 3853 - She brings out the peg when she has ... and hides it when she ...
And «watt» by replacing the dāl with tāʾ and then assimilating the tāʾ into it. This is irregular, because the original is replacing the first for the second, not the reverse. Something like this has preceded in Āl ʿImrān at the saying of Allah the Exalted: {فَمَن زُحْزِحَ عَنِ النار} [Āl ʿImrān: 185]. One says: watid wātid, that is: strong, firm, which is like the figurative saying shughl shāghil. Al-Aṣmaʿī recited:
3854 - She found at the water a firm (wātid) tree-stump, and he would not fail her in the appointments
It was also said: the pegs here are literal, not metaphorical. In tafsīr: that he had pegs to which he tied people, torturing them thereby. The disagreement about al-Ayka has preceded in Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {أولئك الأحزاب}: it may be resumptive with no position, and it may be a khabar. The mubtadaʾ, Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "from His saying «وعادٌ»; it may be from «ثمود»; and it may be from His saying «وقومُ لوط»." I say: the apparent is the conjunction of «عادٌ» and what follows it to «قومُ نوحٍ», and the resumption of the sentence after it. On what Abū al-Baqāʾ said, it would also be permissible that the mubtadaʾ be «وأصحابُ الأَيْكَة» alone.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {إِن كُلٌّ}: «إنْ» is negative and has no operation here at all, not even in the dialect of the one who said:
3854 - bi-in huwa mustawliyan ʿalā aḥadin ... [incomplete in the source]
nor on the reading {إِنَّ الذين تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ الله عِبَاداً}, because the negation is broken by «إلاَّ»; for its being broken in the case of the original, which is «ما», invalidates it, so how with its derivative? It has preceded that it may be an answer to the oath.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {مَّا لَهَا مِن فَوَاقٍ}: «لها» may govern «مِنْ فَواق» as agent in the nominative, relying on the negation; and it may be a sentence of a mubtadaʾ and khabar. On both estimations the negated sentence is accusative in position as an adjective of «صَيْحةً», and «مِنْ» is redundant. The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «فُواق» with ḍamma on the fāʾ, and the rest with fatḥa. It was said that they are two dialects with one meaning, namely the time between two milkings of the milker and two suckings of the suckler; the meaning: "it has no pause of the length of a fuwāq of a she-camel." In the ḥadīth: «العِيادَةُ قَدْرَ فُواقِ ناقة» (the visit to the sick is the length of a fuwāq of a she-camel), and this in meaning is like the saying of Allah the Exalted: {فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمْ لاَ يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ سَاعَةً} [al-Aʿrāf: 34]. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "It has no return." From afāqa l-marīḍ: when he returned to his health. The ifāqa of the she-camel is the moment when the milk returns to her udder. One says: afāqat al-nāqa tufīqu ifāqatan: she returned, and the fīqa gathered in her udder. The fīqa is the milk that gathers between the two milkings, and its plural is afwāq. As for afāwīq, it is the plural of the plural. One says: nāqa mufīq and mufīqa. It was also said: fawāq with fatḥa is the ifāqa and rest, like jawāb from ajāba. Muʾarrij al-Sadūsī and al-Farrāʾ said it, and among the commentators Ibn Zayd and al-Suddī. As for the one with ḍamma, it is a noun, not a maṣdar. The well-known view is that they have one meaning, like qiṣāṣ [al-shaʿr] and quṣāṣ, and ḥamām al-makkūk and ḥumām.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {قِطَّنَا}: that is: "our share and portion." Its origin is from qaṭṭa l-shayʾa, that is: he cut it; from it qaṭṭa l-qalam (he cut the pen). The meaning: a cut from what You promised us. For this reason it is applied to a document and a deed, qiṭṭ, because they are two pieces cut off. A prize is also called qiṭṭ, because it is a piece of the gift. Al-Aʿshā said:
3855 - Nor was al-Nuʿmān the king, on the day you met him in his felicity, giving the qiṭāṭ (grants) and ...
And its most frequent use is for the written document. Umayya said:
3856 - A people who have the courtyard, the land of Iraq, and what is collected to them in it, and the qiṭṭ and the pen
Its plural is quṭūṭ as preceded, and qiṭaṭa, like qird, qirada and qurūd. In the paucal, aqiṭṭa and aqṭāṭ / like qadaḥ, aqdiḥa and aqdāḥ, except that afʿila in the pattern fiʿl is irregular.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {دَاوُودَ}: a badal or ʿaṭf bayān, or accusative by an implied "I mean." And «ذا الأيْدِ» is an adjective of it. Al-ayd is strength. One says: rajul ayd and ayād.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {يُسَبِّحْنَ}: a circumstantial clause from «الجبال». He brought it as an imperfect verb rather than an active participle, not saying musabbiḥāt, to indicate renewal and occurrence bit by bit, as in the saying of al-Aʿshā:
3857 - By my life, many eyes have been drawn to the light of a fire on a height, being burned
that is: being burned bit by bit. Had he said muḥarraqa, it would not have indicated this meaning.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {والطير مَحْشُورَةً}: the majority read both in the accusative: an object conjoined to an object and a ḥāl to a ḥāl, as you say: "I struck Zayd bound and ʿAmr free." He brought the ḥāl as a noun because he did not intend that the action took place bit by bit, since gathering them all at once is a stronger indication of power, and the gatherer is Allah the Exalted. Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Jaḥdarī read both in the nominative, making them an independent sentence of mubtadaʾ and khabar.
His saying: «كُلٌّ له»: that is: each of the mountains and the birds, for Dāwūd, that is: for the sake of his glorification, is a glorifier; so he put «أوَّاب» in place of musabbiḥ. It was also said: the pronoun refers to the Creator, the Exalted, and what is meant is that each of Dāwūd, the mountains and the birds is a glorifier and one who turns back to Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {وَشَدَدْنَا}: the majority read «شَدَدْنا» without tashdīd, that is: "We strengthened," like «سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بأخيك». Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Ḥasan read «شَدَّدْنا» with tashdīd, which is an intensive of the reading of the majority.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {نَبَأُ الخصم}: it has already preceded that al-khaṣm is in origin a maṣdar, so it suits the singular and the masculine and their opposites, and it may also agree [in number]. From it: {لاَ تَخَفْ خَصْمَانِ} [Ṣād: 22] and {هذان خَصْمَانِ} [al-Ḥajj: 19]. What is meant by al-khaṣm here is a plural, by the evidence of His saying «إذ تَسَوَّرُوا» and His saying «إذ دَخَلُوا». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It occurs for the singular and the plural, like al-ḍayf. He the Exalted said: {حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ المكرمين} [al-Dhāriyāt: 24] because it is in origin a maṣdar. One says khaṣamahu yakhṣimuhu khaṣman, as you say ḍāfahu ḍayfan. If you say: this is a plural and His saying «خصمان» is a dual, how is that sound? I say: the meaning of khaṣmān: two parties, two adversaries, and the evidence for it is the reading of those who read «[خَصْمَانِ] بغى بَعْضُهُمْ على بَعْضٍ»; like it is the saying of the Exalted {هذان خَصْمَانِ اختصموا}. If you say: what do you do with His saying {إِنَّ هَذَآ أَخِي}, which is evidence of two? I say: this is the saying of one of them, and what is meant is {بَعْضُنَا على بَعْضٍ}. If you say: there has come in the report that two angels were sent to him? I say: its meaning is that the dispute for judgment was between two angels, and that does not prevent others accompanying them. If you say: how did He name them all 'adversary' in His saying «نَبَأ الخَصْمِ» and «خَصْمان»? I say: since each of the two litigants was accompanied in the form of an adversary, naming by it is sound."
His saying: «إذ تَسَوَّروا»: on what governs «إذ» there are several views. One: that it is governed by «النبأ» when the story is not meant by it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya, Abū al-Baqāʾ and Makkī held this; that is: "Has there come to you the news that occurred at the time of their climbing into the prayer chamber?" Some have rejected this: the news occurring at that time cannot have come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and if the story is meant by the news, it would not be a governor. The Shaykh said it. The second: that the governor is «أتاك», and it is rejected by what rejected the first. Al-Zamakhsharī explicitly rejected these two views, saying: "If you say: by what is «إذ» put in the accusative? I say: it cannot but be put in the accusative by «أتاك», or by «النبأ», or by an omitted element. It is not permissible to put it in the accusative by «أتاك», because the coming of the news to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ occurs only in his time, not in the time of Dāwūd; nor by «النبأ», because the news occurred in the time of Dāwūd, so its coming to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is not sound. And if you mean by the news the story itself, it would not be a governor. So it remains that it is accusative by an omitted element, its estimation: 'and has there come to you the news of the litigation of the adversaries when'." So he chose that it be governed by an omitted element. «[Translator's note: the source text as it stands lists the first, second and fourth views; the third is not present.]» The fourth: that it be put in the accusative by «الخصم» because of the sense of the verb in it.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {إِذْ دَخَلُواْ}: there are two views on it. One: that it is a badal from the first «إذ». The second: that it is accusative by «تَسَوَّرُوا». The meaning of tasawwarū: they climbed / to the top of the sūr, which is the wall, not hamzated, as in your saying tasannama l-baʿīr, that is: he reached its hump (sanām). The pronoun in «تَسَوَّروا» and «دخلوا» refers to the khaṣm because it is a plural in meaning as preceded, or on the basis that it is a dual, and the dual is a plural in meaning; the disagreement about this has already been verified.
His saying: «خَصْمان»: the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "we are two adversaries"; for this reason He said «بَعْضُنا». Whoever read «بعضهم» in the third person may permit estimating it so, having regard to the wording of «خَصْمان», and may permit estimating "they are two adversaries" for agreement. It is reported from al-Kisāʾī «خِصْمان» with kasra on the khāʾ. It has preceded that he read it so in al-Ḥajj.
His saying: «بَغَى بَعْضُنا»: a sentence that may be explicative of their state, and may be a second khabar.
His saying: «ولا تُشْطِطْ»: the majority read with ḍamma on the tāʾ, sukūn on the shīn and kasra on the first ṭāʾ, from ashṭaṭa yushṭiṭu ishṭāṭan, when he transgressed the truth. Abū ʿUbayda said: "shaṭaṭtu fī l-ḥukm and ashṭaṭtu fīhi, when I was unjust"; so it is among those in which faʿala and afʿala coincide. He uncontracted it on one of the two permissible ways, as in «مَنْ يَرْتَدِدْ», and its verification has preceded. Al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «تَشْطُط» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the ṭāʾ, from shaṭṭa in the sense of ashaṭṭa as preceded. Qatāda read «تُشِطَّ», from the quadriliteral ashaṭṭa, except that he assimilated, which is one of the two permissible ways, like the reading of those who read {مَن يَرْتَدَّ مِنكُمْ}; and from him also «تُشَطِّطْ» with fatḥa on the shīn and kasra on the ṭāʾ with tashdīd, shaṭṭaṭa yushaṭṭiṭu; the intensification in it is for increase. Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh read «تُشاطِطْ», of the pattern mufāʿala.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا}: «كم» is the object of «أهلَكْنا», «مِنْ قَرْنٍ» is a tamyīz, and «مِنْ قبلِهم» is for the beginning of the range.
His saying: «ولات حين»: this sentence is accusative in position as a ḥāl from the agent of «نادَوْا», that is: they cried for help, while there was no escape and no deliverance.
The majority read «لاتَ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and «حينَ» in the accusative, and there are several views on it.
